faq.a: Sardar is associated with the Persian form سَرْدَار, whose core sense is sardar; commander, chief (persian/kurdish).

faq.q: What is the origin of Sardar?
faq.a: Sardar is associated with Persian. Sardar is Persian سردار (sardār), meaning 'commander, chief'. It is used as a male given name in Kurdistan, Iran and South Asia.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Sardar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sardar should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sardār is a Persian word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Sardar mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sardar is rendered سردار and carries the sense سردار، سردار.

faq.q: What does Sardar mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sardar is rendered سردار and carries the sense سردار، فرمانده.
A romanized syllable approximation is sar-dar. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sardar?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sardar, sardar. Script forms are سردار, سَرْدَار, सरदार.

faq.q: Is Sardar a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
